decisions.statement: A call naming no argument reads the past twenty-four hours.
A run is one deploy measured around the whole call that put the thing up.
The rows are read from beside the page of the thing put up.
Every kind a deploy puts up is reached through the index rather than a folder named here.
A kind put up whole is reached at the page type naming that kind.
A list built from the pages of each kind alone misses that one set of rows.
Every numbered file of those rows is read rather than the first alone.
Only the entries beside such a page are read.
A check spells the same phase into its own logs and no such log is read here.
A row naming the deploy phase is read and no other row is.
The runs are gathered under what the row says ran.
A file that would not read is named rather than counting as no runs.
A row a write left half appended is passed over and the rest of the file read.
A page holding no run of what was chosen is not listed at all.
The total counts the distinct runs read rather than the records read.
The total shares the processor time over the distinct runs read.
The total draws its average memory as `-`.
A run's processor time is that run's own together with the children it reaped.
A run's memory is what that run added over the memory resident when it opened.
A run that noted no high-water mark is left out of the memory reported.
What was put up is ordered by what its runs took on average.
Two taking equal processor time are ordered by name.
A run writes no value the commit has.
Nothing here puts anything up.
An argument this command does not take is refused.

definition: the command saying what putting a thing up cost in processor time and memory
